text:
Josh: Thinking out loud — proposal to add a 'microstep failover attenuator' to canary ramps so tiny early cohorts can automatically shift traffic to a stable fallback variant if errors or latency spike. Draft API sketch below, looking for reactions and edge cases.

Lina: Quick question — what counts as a 'spike'? rolling error-rate over 1m vs 5m? p50 vs p99? And do we scope this per-region/slice? :thinking_face:

Sam: API naming nit: prefer a single semantic like safety_policy with trigger/action subfields. "attenuator" ok internally, but public surface should read clearly: safety_policy: { trigger: ..., action: ... } so future trigger types fit.

Taylor: Telemetry note: we should use a composite signal to avoid noisy flips. e.g. (error_rate > X OR p99_latency > Y) AND error_budget_burn > Z. Also require a cooldown window and backoff.

Marta: From a UX defaults perspective keep microsteps short and tiny: 0.5% for 5m, 2% for 10m, then 10% for 20m. If attenuation happens, the console should mark rollout state as 'attenuated' with a one-line reason and a link to the triggering metrics.

Josh: Draft config (working example):
```yaml
canary:
  steps:
    - pct: 0.5
      duration: 5m
    - pct: 2
      duration: 10m
    - pct: 10
      duration: 20m
  safety_policy:
    trigger:
      error_rate_rolling: {window: 1m, threshold: 0.02} # 2%
      p99_latency_ms: 1200
      combine_with: "or"
    action:
      mode: "hard" # hard | soft
      attenuate_to_variant: "v1-stable"
      attenuate_pct: 0.0 # fully divert
      soft_divert_fraction: 0.2 # used when mode=soft
      min_soft_divert_pct: 0.5
      cooldown: 15m
      mark_state: "attenuated"
```

Sam: Agree on the schema. Couple additions: make combine_with an enum (or/and/hybrid). For soft mode, compute diverted pct as max(traffic * soft_divert_fraction, min_soft_divert_pct). Also add per-candidate cooldown enforced by runtime to avoid oscillation (circuit-breaker behavior).

Lina: We must scope triggers per-routing-slice (region, customer tier). A global metric could be dominated by one region's flake. Triggers need a slice key so the console can show which slice caused the attenuator.

Taylor: Yes — emit an attenuation event with metadata: model, version, slice, trigger_reason, metrics_snapshot. That makes debugging and postmortem easier. Also surface error_budget_burn in the rollout object so thresholds can be computed automatically.

Marta: UX question: should users be allowed to manually resume an attenuated rollout? I say yes, but require an explicit override checkbox and create an audit log entry. Also show a warning if the rollout exceeded error budget previously.

Josh: Implementation plan: I'll open a PR with the schema changes, console copy for attenuated state, and a tiny runtime circuit-breaker that enforces cooldown and soft/hard behavior. Will include example configs and a dry-run job. Assigning to myself and will loop in telemetry/ops for the metric tags.

deploy-bot: [simulation] dry-run scheduled for rollout "redwood/model-x:v2" — estimated attenuation chance: 14%. Job id: dryrun-2123456790

Sam: Please include unit + integration tests that simulate flaky downstreams to validate cooldown, per-slice behavior, and soft-mode partial diversion. Also add e2e for audit logs and console state transitions.

Josh: Will do. I'll post the PR link when ready and add a simulated-dryrun that runs against 7d historical metrics so teams can tune thresholds before rollout. Thanks all :raised_hands:
